D018-D013_h001.question:
I’ve been struggling for about six months now—since that day I responded to the downtown courthouse shooting as part of our city emergency protocol. I didn’t think it would stick with me like this, but sometimes, out of nowhere, I’m right back there—the sirens, the shouting, the blood. I freeze. My hands shake. It’s like I’m not here. 

I don’t go fishing anymore, which I used to love. My wife notices. I just don’t feel like doing much. I even snapped at my coworker the other day, blaming him for not sending a report on time, though I know it wasn’t really his fault. I can’t shake the feeling that if someone had just acted faster that day, things might’ve been different. 

I startle at loud noises—doors slamming, phones ringing. My heart races and doesn’t let up. Choosing what to wear, what to eat… I stand there, frozen. It’s exhausting. I feel heavy, down, but I can’t say if it’s from that day, or just life, or both. I don’t cry. I don’t sleep poorly every night. It’s just… a fog, most days.
D018-D013_h001.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
D018-D013_h001.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h002.question:
I’ve been off since last semester—kind of fading in and out, really. There was this incident at a party, something I don’t like to talk about… but sometimes, it feels like I’m right back there. Out of nowhere, a loud laugh or a slammed door and I’m jolted—heart racing, like I’m trapped all over again. It’s not constant, but it happens enough that I avoid big groups now. I used to hang out with my dorm mates, go to study sessions, but now I just stay in my room. Feels safer.

I keep thinking it was my fault—like I should’ve left earlier or said something. I know people tell me it wasn’t, but that doesn’t make it stop. I can’t focus in lecture; my mind drifts, and I’ll read the same paragraph three times and still not get it. I’m tired all the time, not sleeping well. Some days I don’t even want to get out of bed, not because I’m sad exactly… just empty. I don’t know if it’s about *that night* or just college stress, or both. It’s been a few months, but I can’t tell if I’m getting better or just used to feeling this way.
D018-D013_h002.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
D018-D013_h002.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h003.question:
I’ve been off since the office evacuation last year—when the alarms went off and the building shook during that incident. I don’t talk about it much, but I keep reliving those seconds: the noise, the panic, people screaming. It pops into my head out of nowhere, especially when there’s a loud sound—construction outside, a phone ringing too hard. I flinch, sometimes so hard I drop things. It’s embarrassing in meetings.  

Lately, nothing feels good, not even things I used to love—weekends with my wife, following the market closings, even food. I just go through the motions. I used to get a rush from closing a big fund deal. Now it means nothing. I can’t focus long enough to read an earnings report all the way through. My mind drifts, or I get tense, like danger’s coming.  

I keep thinking it could’ve been avoided—if certain people had acted faster, if protocols were followed. I know I shouldn’t fixate, but I do. And the fear? It hasn’t lessened. It still feels raw, like it happened yesterday. I’m not sure if I’m depressed or just… stuck. It’s affecting everything, but I can’t pinpoint when it crossed a line.
D018-D013_h003.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
D018-D013_h003.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h004.question:
I’ve been having a hard time since… well, since that incident in the courtroom last year. I don’t like talking about it, but sometimes just hearing a door slam the wrong way makes my chest tighten and my hands go numb. It’s like I’m back there, and I can’t catch my breath. I’ve started keeping my office door cracked so no one can walk in without warning—sudden movements just throw me. I forget things too, like where I put files or even appointments. I used to be so sharp; now I feel scattered.

Work’s been harder. I don’t feel like taking on new cases, even though I know they need me. It’s not that I don’t care—I do—but it feels pointless sometimes. I keep thinking, *why did no one step in? Why did the judge let it go that far?* It wasn’t my fault, but I carry it like it is. I feel… small, like I should’ve handled it differently. I’ve had moments wondering if I’m even cut out for this job anymore. I used to be passionate. Now I just feel heavy. I don’t know if this is from what happened, or if I was already headed here and that moment just cracked something open.
D018-D013_h004.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
D018-D013_h004.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h005.question:
I’ve been struggling for about six months now—maybe longer, it’s hard to tell. Things just feel… heavy. I’m the principal of a high school, so I’m used to being on, making decisions, supporting teachers and kids, but lately I’ve had to force myself through the day. There’s this constant pressure in my chest, like anger I can’t let out, and I snap at people over small things—my staff, my husband—then feel awful after. 

There are certain things—like a specific sound, or someone touching my shoulder from behind—that make me jolt or feel instantly on edge. I’ve stopped going to staff luncheons or even meeting friends. I just don’t want to talk. Sometimes I zone out during meetings, thoughts foggy, like I’m not fully there. 

After what happened at the school last year—the incident with the student—it just changed how I see everything. I keep thinking if only certain people had acted differently, it wouldn’t have gone so far. I know that might not be fair, but in my head, it feels true. I’m tired all the time, but I can’t say whether it’s from not sleeping, or from carrying this weight.
D018-D013_h005.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
D018-D013_h005.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h006.question:
I’ve been off since the accident last year—the car crash. I don’t know, maybe nine months ago? It’s fuzzy. Some parts I remember too clearly, like the sound of metal crushing, but other parts—like right before it happened—just… blank. Sometimes, out of nowhere, I’m back there. My chest tightens, I can’t breathe, like I’m behind the wheel again. It only lasts a few seconds, but I’ve dropped things, startled my husband. He learned not to touch me from behind—he tried to surprise me once, just a hand on my shoulder, and I jumped so hard I knocked over a lamp.  

I don’t feel like I used to. I love my husband, I *know* I do, but it’s like the feeling’s muffled, like there’s glass between us. I avoid talking about the crash—anything close to it. Therapy asked me to go over it, and I shut down. Can’t.  

There’s been yelling. Once, I threw my phone across the room when my husband asked what was wrong. I didn’t hurt him, but I could feel the rage boiling.  

I’m tired all the time. Not sleeping well. I don’t know if it’s the crash, or just… everything.
D018-D013_h006.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h006.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h007.question:
I’ve been off for about six months, maybe a bit longer—ever since that storm chaser incident out in Kansas. I wasn’t even in the direct path, but... I keep finding myself back there. Sometimes I’m in the middle of it—the wind, the roar, the radio cutting out—and I’ll snap out of it while I’m standing in the kitchen, holding a coffee mug that’s been empty for twenty minutes. I don’t talk about it much. My wife tries, but I shut down. It’s easier not to go there.

I can’t remember chunks of what happened during the storm. Blank, just static. And even when I got awarded for the forecasting model last month—the one that actually helped save lives—I didn’t feel anything. My wife said I looked like I were at a funeral.

The little things set me off now. A car backfires, and I’m ducking. I threw a tablet across the room last week when the alert alarm went off during a briefing. I didn’t mean to, but the noise punched through me. I’ve been short with everyone—my team, my wife. I’m tired all the time, but it’s not just sleep. It’s like I’m underwater.
D018-D013_h007.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h007.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h008.question:
I’ve been off for a while now—about six months, give or take. Ever since that night at the plant… you know, when the press malfunctioned and we lost two guys. I remember bits of it—the red warning light flashing, someone shouting, the sound of metal buckling—but other parts? Gone. Blank. Like a tape cut in the middle.  

Since then, I can’t stand loud noises. A dropped wrench, a slammed door—it makes me jump, heart racing, like I’m back there. I’ve been avoiding the safety reports, the meetings where they review incidents. Just looking at them tightens my chest. My wife says I’m distant. I don’t argue, but I don’t feel much either. It’s like I’m watching life from behind glass. Laughter, worry, even anger—most days, nothing gets through.  

I snap easy, though. Too easy. My foreman said I’ve been riding people too hard on the line. But I can’t seem to stop. Nerves feel raw all the time. I don’t sleep. Just lie there, wired.  

I don’t know if it’s grief over what happened, or if I’m just… broken now. Some days I feel low, drained, like I’m dragging weight. But I can’t tell if that’s from the accident, or just life.
D018-D013_h008.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h008.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h009.question:
I’ve been off-kilter for months—maybe longer. It’s like parts of me are missing. I design jewelry, so I need steady hands and focus, but lately, I’ll be shaping metal and suddenly feel… gone. Like I’m not at my bench anymore. Once, I dropped a file and just froze, back in that hotel room from years ago—smell of smoke, the yelling. It’s not real, but I feel it. Afterward, my hands shake for ages. I can’t calm down.  

I don’t talk about what happened. I don’t even let myself go there. Whole chunks of that time? Blank. I know something bad was, but details slip away. It’s easier that way.  

I sold a collection last month—big gallery, nice write-up. Normally, that’d make my week. But I just felt hollow. My assistant was thrilled for me, and I smiled, but inside? Nothing.  

I snap at people—my assistant, my daughter—over tiny things. Then I feel bad, but the anger’s always simmering, like I’m guarding against something. I don’t know if it’s this grief or… trauma or both. I don’t know what this is, really. Some days it feels tied to the past. Other days, it’s just a weight I can’t name.
D018-D013_h009.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h009.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h010.question:
I’ve been off my usual rhythm for about six months now, ever since that accident on the job—tree came down wrong, nearly got me. I wasn’t seriously hurt, but something changed. I can’t go near chainsaws anymore. Just the sound of one starting up makes my chest tighten, my hands shake. I’ve asked coworkers to switch routes if we’re going to prune near that property. Even seeing a chainsaw in a toolbox out here on site… I just need to walk away.

I remember pieces of the fall—the crack, the blur of motion—but some parts are just gone. Not sure if it’s shock or what. And honestly, even when things go well—like when a client compliments a design I planted—I don’t feel it. No pride, no joy. Just… flat.

I snap sometimes. Last week, a guy bumped a wheelbarrow into me by accident and I yelled like he attacked me. Felt bad after, but I couldn’t calm down—heart kept hammering, face hot, like I was back in it. Takes me ages to settle once I’m rattled. I don’t sleep well. Don’t really want to talk about it. I just keep working, but it’s harder to care.
D018-D013_h010.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h010.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h011.question:
I’ve been struggling for about a year now—ever since that incident on the bus. I don’t like talking about it, but sometimes just seeing a similar bus route or hearing loud voices makes my chest tighten. I avoid that part of the city entirely, and I stopped going to the study center because one of the instructors reminded me of someone who was there that day. It’s not that I think he was involved, but just his presence… it’s too much.  

I get angry easily now. The smallest thing—like someone asking me what’s wrong—sets me off. I’ve snapped at my mom, cursed at classmates. I don’t mean to, but it’s like the frustration just explodes.  

I don’t know if anything really matters anymore. I used to believe in working hard, in passing the exam and serving my community, but now it all feels pointless. Like the world doesn’t care who gets hurt. I keep thinking, *Why bother preparing for a future when anything can be taken in a second?*  

I’ve lost interest in my study groups. I sleep too much or not at all. But I’m not sure if this is grief, burnout, or something deeper. Some days I think it’s trauma. Other days, it feels more like I’m just… sinking.
D018-D013_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D018-D013_h011.answer: A & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h012.question:
I’ve been having these moments—sudden, like I’m back there again. I’ll be in the cab, quiet, just running the line, and suddenly I’m not in the train anymore. I see the platform, the faces, that one guy who fell… I can’t move, can’t speak for a second. Then it’s over, but my hands shake. I don’t like talking about it—any of it. The department wanted me to debrief, but I said no. Thinking about it just pulls it all up again, and I can’t afford that when I’m on duty.

People keep saying, “It wasn’t your fault,” but they don’t get it. They just talk. I don’t trust anyone lately—not coworkers, not even other drivers. Feels like everyone’s careless, like they’d just look away if something happened. I blame management, honestly. They cut training, won’t install the platform doors... they knew this could happen.

Little things set me off—someone late on the radio, a delay, even someone looking at me wrong. I snapped at my wife last week over nothing. Just yelled. She didn’t deserve that. I’ve been low, sleeping poorly, not enjoying much. But I don’t know if it’s the job, the incident, or just... me.
D018-D013_h012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D018-D013_h012.answer: A & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h013.question:
I’ve been having these moments—like I’m back there again. Not all the time, just every now and then. It might be a sound, or someone saying something offhand, and suddenly I’m not in the room anymore. Last week, a server alarm at work beeped in this certain rhythm, and I was right back in the emergency room that night my wife passed. I couldn’t speak for a minute. Just stood there. It’s gone quickly now, but it used to last longer.

I don’t go by the hospital much anymore. Haven’t visited her grave in months. It’s not that I don’t want to—it just… pulls something loose. And I’ve stopped talking to most of the people from back then. Old friends, her family. Seems easier.

I keep thinking I should’ve seen it coming. She said she wasn’t feeling well, but I told her it was just stress. I was fixing a payroll system that afternoon. I should’ve taken her in.

People say things like “time heals,” but I don’t know. I snap sometimes—yelled at a junior developer over a syntax error last month. Didn’t mean to. I just… feel on edge, like I’m waiting for the next failure to hit.  
 
Some days I stay in bed. Not because I’m sad, really—more like there’s no point switching on the lights.
D018-D013_h013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D018-D013_h013.answer: A & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h014.question:
I’ve been having these flashes—random moments when I’m back there, like I can see it all again, hear the sounds, feel my heart slamming. It happens out of nowhere, even while I’m at work handing someone their latte. I try not to think about it, push it down, but then I get this tightness in my chest and I just want to disappear. I don’t talk about it, not with anyone. Even when my roommate checks in, I say I’m fine.  

The world feels… off now. Like, nothing really matters, and people can’t be trusted—they don’t get it, they won’t help. Sometimes I blame others, like if they’d just done one thing differently, maybe none of it would’ve happened. I snapped at a customer last week, threw a cup down when they raised their voice. Not proud of it, but it just exploded.  

I’m tired all the time, not sleeping right, and some days I can’t get out of bed. I don’t know if it’s from what happened, or just… life. I don’t even know when it started blending together.
D018-D013_h014.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D018-D013_h014.answer: A & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h015.question:
I’ve been having a tough time the past few months—maybe longer. There’s this weight I can’t shake, like I’m constantly replaying something I’d rather forget. A few years back, I was in a bad car accident—nobody made it out unscathed. Sometimes just seeing flashing lights or hearing tires screech throws me off completely. I start sweating, my chest tightens—it’s like I’m right back there.  

Since then, I don’t talk about it much. I avoid driving that stretch of road, and I don’t let myself really think about what happened. But the thoughts sneak in anyway, especially at night. I keep wondering if I could’ve done something differently—if I’d taken a different route or left earlier. Now I feel like I’m broken in a way most people wouldn’t understand. Like I don’t trust myself anymore.  

I’ve snapped at coworkers over small things—emails, missed deadlines—stuff that wouldn’t have bothered me before. It’s not like I’m angry all the time, but when it hits, it comes out of nowhere. I don’t feel like myself, but I’m not sure what’s from the accident and what’s just… me lately. I can still get through the workday, but everything feels heavier.
D018-D013_h015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D018-D013_h015.answer: A & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h016.question:
I’ve been having these flashes—like out of nowhere—of that day on my route when the dog attacked me. I see it in my sleep, sometimes in the middle of the day while I’m walking. It’s not just the bite, it’s the sound, the blood, how fast it happened. Ever since, I’ve started taking different streets, even if it adds miles. I can’t go near that house, not even by accident. 

I catch myself scanning every yard now, watching for movement, checking where the exits are in a room. My wife says I’m “on alert” all the time. And honestly? I blame the owner. Just left that dog loose. No warning, no care. That wouldn’t have happened if he’d done his part.

Lately, things feel heavy. I don’t laugh like I used to. Even small stuff—coffee, the radio, seeing my kids—feels distant. I keep going because I have to, but some mornings, getting out of the truck takes everything. It’s been months, but I can’t say it’s constant. Some days are okay. Not great. But okay.
D018-D013_h016.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h016.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h017.question:
I’ve been having these dreams—nightmares, really—about the emergency landing from last year. Not every night, but often enough that I dread sleep. The cockpit, the alarms, the way the passengers screamed… it all comes back, and I wake up drenched in sweat, heart pounding like I’m back in it. Since then, I’ve stopped flying that route. I even turned down a training session in the same aircraft model—just couldn’t bring myself to go near it. It feels weak, I know, but the thought of being reminded... it’s too much.  

Lately, I keep thinking—what if I’d reacted faster? Maybe I could’ve prevented some of the panic. It wasn’t just mechanical failure; people got hurt. I was in control, and now I wonder if I failed them.  

At hotels or airports, I always sit facing the door. I scan the exits, watch people’s hands, listen for sudden noises. My wife says I’m too alert, like I’m never really off duty. I just want to feel safe, but it’s hard when my mind keeps circling back.  

I’m not sleeping well, feel heavy most days, and I’ve lost interest in things I used to enjoy—dinner with my wife, even flying for fun. But I can’t say if that’s from the incident, the stress, or just… getting older. Some days are okay. Others aren’t.
D018-D013_h017.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h017.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h018.question:
I’ve been feeling off since the break-in at the restaurant last year—sometimes it hits me hard when I see someone loitering outside, or when the door slams suddenly. I get this wave of panic, like it’s happening all over again, and I have to step into the back office just to catch my breath. I don’t like talking about it, even with my husband. Thinking too much about that night just pulls me down, so I try not to go there.  

There were a couple of guys who knew about the safe—they’d been in before as customers. I can’t help but think they could’ve stopped it, or even warned us. It’s not fair that we had to go through that while others just walked away.  

Now I check the locks three times before closing. I scan the room when I’m serving—where are the exits, who looks out of place. It doesn’t feel like fear, not exactly. More like I’m just… making sure.  

The joy’s gone from things, honestly. I used to love cooking for big weekends, but now I just get through the shift. I haven’t told anyone at home how empty I feel—like I’m just going through motions. But is that from what happened? Or just life? I don’t know anymore.
D018-D013_h018.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h018.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h019.question:
I’ve been struggling lately—hard to shake the memories of what happened during that home showing last year, the break-in. It just pops into my head at the worst times, like when I’m trying to sleep or when I’m showing a quiet house. I can’t stop thinking about why I didn’t notice the signs, why I let my client walk in first. I beat myself up constantly—I should’ve known, I should’ve done something.  

Because of that, I’ve been avoiding certain neighborhoods, even if the listing is perfect. I just can’t bring myself to go there. Sometimes I cancel viewings last minute if I see the address. I know it’s affecting my work, but I can’t help it.  

And now I’m always on high alert. I scan every room, check exits, notice anything odd—a loose window, a shadow—my pulse spikes. It’s exhausting.  

I don’t feel like myself. I’m withdrawn, not sleeping well, not as present with my husband. But I can’t tell if it’s the trauma or just… life. It’s been months, but I don’t know if this is PTSD, depression, or just me trying to move through something hard.
D018-D013_h019.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h019.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h020.question:
Lately, I’ve been feeling like I’m not fully here—sometimes I’ll be mid-sentence on air and suddenly feel like I’m back in that parking garage, heart racing, like it’s happening all over again. It’s not a memory; it’s like I’m *in* it. Afterward, I’ll realize I’ve blanked for a few seconds, and my producer gives me that look. I don’t talk about that night—not with friends, not in therapy. It’s easier if I don’t go there at all.  

I keep thinking I should’ve taken a different route, left earlier. It’s my fault. Logically, I know that’s not fair, but it doesn’t stop the weight behind my ribs when I wake up at 3 a.m., listening too closely to every sound in my apartment—like something’s coming. I can’t sit with my back to the door anymore.  

Some days, everything feels heavy. I cancel brunches, ignore texts. I still show up, do the job, smile on cue. But inside, I’m either numb or bracing for impact. I don’t know if it’s grief, fear, or something else entirely—just that I can’t seem to land.
D018-D013_h020.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h020.answer: C & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h021.question:
I’ve been struggling for several months now—maybe longer. Things that never bothered me before just set me off. A sound, a smell, even something someone says—out of nowhere, my chest tightens and I feel like I’m back in that moment, though I can’t—and don’t want to—fully remember it. It’s not constant, but when it happens, it’s like a switch flips. I get angry—no, not just angry—there’s this heat inside, like I’ve been simmering for years and no achievement at work, no compliment from my husband, nothing, cools it down. I got praised during tax season—the first time in years I actually finished on time and felt I did a good job—but I remember sitting at dinner that night, staring at my plate, thinking, *So what?* No pride, no relief. Just hollow.  

Lately, I snap at my team over tiny mistakes. I don’t mean to—sometimes I don’t even realize how sharp I was until they flinch. My husband says I’m “on edge all the time,” like I’m waiting for something bad to happen. I don’t cry much. I just feel… tight. Worn down. But I can’t say if this all started because of one big thing, or if it’s just life wearing me down. I don’t know anymore what’s cause and what’s effect.
D018-D013_h021.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h021.answer: B & A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h022.question:
I’ve been having these dreams—over and over—about *that night*. It’s never the same, but it always ends with me feeling like I can’t breathe. I wake up drenched, heart pounding, and it takes forever to remember I’m in my own bed. My husband says I’ve been pulling away. I don’t mean to, but it’s like there’s this wall inside me now. Things that used to make me happy—music, even little work wins—just… don’t land. It’s like I’m watching life from behind glass.

And the anger? It’s always simmering. Little things set me off—traffic, a misread email, even how he loads the dishwasher. I snap. Yell. Say things I don’t mean. Then I feel awful, but it’s like I can’t stop the wave once it starts. I know I’m not myself. I love my job—digging into how people interact with design—but lately, even that feels heavy. I go through the motions, but my focus slips, and I’m exhausted all the time.

It’s been months. Maybe half a year? I can’t say if this is from what happened or just… me shutting down. I don’t feel broken exactly—just hollow. And furious. All at once.
D018-D013_h022.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h022.answer: B & A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h023.question:
I’ve been having these moments—snapshots, really—where I’m back in that alley again. It’s not like remembering; it’s like *being* there. Last week, during roll call, the smell of burnt rubber from a car outside hit me and suddenly I could feel the weight of my gear, the radio crackling, like it was happening all over. It only lasts seconds, but it’s real.  

Since then, I can’t look my wife in the eye without feeling this deep shame, like I failed somehow—even though she tells me I didn’t. I want to hold her, to mean it, but it’s like the switch is off. I don’t feel hate, just… nothing.  

And the anger—I didn’t used to be like this. Last Sunday, my partner nudged my coffee mug, and I shouted like he’d hit me. No warning. I see it in their faces now, the hesitation. I’ve pulled back at work because I don’t trust myself.  

Sleep’s shot. I’m tired, sure, and things feel heavy, but I can’t say if it’s from the event, or just… life. I show up. I do the job. But I don’t know who I am anymore.
D018-D013_h023.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h023.answer: B & A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h024.question:
I’ve been having these flashbacks—like, outta nowhere. I’ll be driving, minding my own business, and suddenly I’m back in that alley behind the gas station, hearing the gunshot, seeing the kid fall. It’s like I can’t shut it off. Some days it’s so real I have to pull over. Makes no sense—it’s been two years, but my brain won’t let it go.

Since then, I don’t know… I feel hollow. My daughter calls, tries to visit, but I can’t hug her like before. I see the hurt in her eyes, and I feel guilty—ashamed, even—that I can’t feel warmth toward my own blood. Like something in me just shut down. I don’t deserve to be loved, not after what I didn’t stop.

And yeah, I lose my temper. Last week I screamed at a passenger for asking me to roll up the window. Cursed him out for no reason. Felt bad after, but the anger just explodes before I can stop it.

I’m tired all the time, but not the kind sleep fixes. Just… dragging. I don’t know if it’s from that night, or if I was already going downhill. Hard to say what came first.
D018-D013_h024.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h024.answer: B & A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder

D018-D013_h025.question:
I’ve been having these dreams… they come and go, not every night, but often enough. I see things from the past—what happened when the house caught fire, my husband trapped, me trying to get back in. The heat, the smoke—I wake up gasping. Sometimes I think I smell it even now.  

It’s hard to feel calm these days. I’m always on edge, like something bad’s about to happen, even when nothing is. I get startled easy—just the phone ringing can make my heart race. And sometimes… I snap. Last week I shouted at my neighbor over a misplaced newspaper. I don’t know why I got so angry. I feel bad afterward, but it just spills out.  

I used to take pride in little things—baking, keeping the house tidy. Now, even when I finish something nice, it feels… empty. I don’t feel good about it. I used to enjoy coffee with my daughter on Sundays, but lately I cancel. Not because I don’t love her—she means everything—but gathering energy to smile, to seem okay, it’s too much.  

I wouldn’t say I’m sad all the time, but… it’s like a weight. It’s been like this, on and off, for months. I thought it would pass, but it hasn’t.
D018-D013_h025.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D013_h025.answer: B & A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Major Depressive Disorder
